title: Meta 发布约 100 克、售价 1300 美元的新 VR 眼镜
content:
Meta announces VR glasses that cost $1,300 and weigh 100 grams
Business
Extended Reality
News
Meta announces new VR glasses that weigh about 100 grams and cost $1,300
There will be new Tetris Effect, Beat Saber, and Ace Attorney games coming to the platform as well.
Diego Argüello
,
Contributing Editor, News
,
GameDeveloper.com
September 24, 2026
schedule
2 Min Read
Image via Meta
Meta has announced the Meta VR Glasses, a new wearable that is set to cost $1,300, weighs about 100 grams, and will feature quite a few prominent game franchises, including Capcom's Ace Attorney.
Officially
introduced yesterday
, the company pitches the device as a pair of glasses you can comfortably wear for hours. There isn't a strap and controllers aren't needed, using capabilities like hand tracking and passthrough to navigate it. There is, however, a puck connected by an optical tether, which handles compute, battery, and storage. Meta expects users to "conveniently" clip to their pocket or bag.
By design, the Meta VR Glasses are not intended solely for games, as most of the announcement is spent talking about how they can be used as a "multi-screen private workspace," as well as featuring an IMAX Enhanced certification and access to US sports events. Yet, there is still a focus on games, which was bolstered by a slate of new announcements.
Related:
Former Avalanche Studios chief Natalie Francis joins Massive Entertainment as managing director
One of the most prominent reveals is
Phoenix Wright Ace Attorney: Dual Destinies VR
, which adapts the fifth mainline entry in the loud lawyer series and further neglects people's desire for a seventh entry. The
trailer
showcases the player making use of hand-tracking gestures to present evidence and point at witnesses to raise objections, with the latter using voice-activation for you to actually shout the word.
There's also
Tetris Effect: Mixed Realities
, which is a hand-controlled and room-aware mixed reality version of
Tetris Effect
, and
Beat Saber: Flux
, which adds hand-tacking to the rhythm game. All three games are slated to launch in 2027, but they aren't exclusive to the Meta VR Glasses and will be available on the Quest as well.
Meta's decision to place video games front-and-center of its new VR headset may surprise some readers, as the actual situation in and around Meta doesn't
paint a pretty picture
. The company's Reality Labs division, which houses its video game business, has
lost around $83.6 billion in six years
after being tasked with wrestling the metaverse into being. During that time, Meta has
shuttered a number of its internal VR studios
—including
Asgard's Wrath
developer Sanzaru Games,
Deadpool VR
maker Twisted Pixel Games, and
Resident Evil 4 VR
developer Armature Studio.
Despite the ongoing climate around VR, companies continue to push for new headsets. A few weeks ago, Valve shared details of the
Steam Frame
, which is a wireless headset with controllers that falls more in line with the Meta Quest 3. At the same time, the device will cost $1,059 for the basic 256GB model, with the 1TB model rounding up to $1,200 instead. And that's without purchasing any additional accessories, like a standalone power cable.
Related:
Irish Game Fund expands with additional funding pathways
The Meta VR Glasses will go on sale on Spring 2027 for $1,300. You can find more information about it on the
official site
.
